title: Abu Talib’s Last Bed • What He Could Not Do • Forty Days Later, Another House • The Year of Sorrow • On the Road to Ta’if • Ten Days of Humiliation

blocks.1: Some time after the siege broke, the tenth year of prophethood. Abu Talib was old, ill. On his deathbed. This man had held the Prophet {{1}} to his chest from the age of eight. He had loved him more than his own sons. Taken him along on journeys, lifted food and fed him. Stood against the whole Quraysh. Stayed three years besieged in the valley, staking his chieftainship and his ties. Yet he did not believe.
blocks.2: The Prophet {{1}} went and sat beside him. He said, uncle, say ‘La ilaha illa Allah’. Just one word; with which I will be able to bear witness for you before Allah.
blocks.3: In the house sat Abu Jahl and ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah too. They said, Abu Talib, in this last age of yours will you give up the religion of ‘Abd al-Muttalib!
blocks.4: The Prophet {{1}} said the same thing again and again. They too said the same thing again and again. In the end the words that came out of Abu Talib’s mouth were: he was on the religion of ‘Abd al-Muttalib. The kalimah he did not say.
blocks.5: From the mouth of the Prophet {{1}} came one thing only; I will ask forgiveness for you, until I am forbidden. In this one scene a great truth of the Sirah is held. The Prophet {{2}} loved people with a real love. His uncle’s death in disbelief made him weep; it gave him no joy. He did not want his uncle to go to Hell. So he tried to the last moment, and wished to make du‘a even after death.
blocks.6: The Prophet {{1}} said, by Allah, until I am forbidden I will keep asking forgiveness for you.{{2}}
blocks.9: (O Prophet!) Surely you cannot guide whom you love; rather Allah guides whom He wills. And He knows best who are the guided.{{1}}
blocks.11: It is not for the Prophet and the believers to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they be relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are people of the Fire.{{1}}
blocks.13: The first verse needs to be read once slowly. ‘You cannot guide whom you love; rather Allah guides whom He wills.’ This is said to the Messenger of Allah. One at whose single recitation the Christian king al-Najashi wept. One at whose one page of Qur’an ‘Umar (RA) went out to kill and came back Muslim.
blocks.14: That very man could not make his own uncle, whom he loved like a father, who had shielded him for forty years, say a single kalimah. Because the work of giving guidance is not the prophet’s. The prophet’s work is to convey. Placing it in the heart is Allah’s.
blocks.15: From here a point for us. Someone at home does not pray, is far from the din; and we, unable to change him, break down. We blame ourselves, think there is a flaw in my effort.
blocks.16: The Prophet {{1}} could not change his uncle. That was no flaw in his effort. Our responsibility is to be beside them, behave well, say the word gently when the chance comes, and make du‘a. To leave the result in Allah’s hands.
blocks.17: The person for whom even the Prophet {{1}} wished to seek forgiveness, even his guidance lay in the end in Allah’s decision. What we can, that much is our work. To torment oneself over the rest is wrong.
blocks.18: What Abu Talib gave the Prophet {{1}} is not little; forty years of refuge, love, standing against the whole Quraysh, a three-year siege. But none of this is a substitute for faith.
blocks.19: Only one thing will be of use in the Hereafter; dying with ‘La ilaha illa Allah’. Relations, favours, lineage; these have value in this world, not on the plain of Qiyamah. The Prophet {{1}} later said, Abu Talib will be in the lightest punishment of Hell; under his two feet two shoes of fire, in which his brain will boil. And he will be the person with the least punishment in Hell.{{2}}
blocks.20: The uncle for whom the Prophet {{1}} did so much, his end too did not change without faith.
blocks.22: Within a couple of months of Abu Talib’s passing, another death. Khadijah bint Khuwaylid (RA). Twenty-five years of companionship. Mother of six children. The day the Prophet {{1}} came home from the cave of Hira trembling, lay down saying ‘cover me with a cloak’; the first person who believed him that day was this Khadijah (RA). She said, Allah will never humiliate you. You maintain the rights of kin, bear the burden of the helpless, serve the guest.
blocks.23: When the whole of Makkah was calling him a liar, one person at home was saying, I know you are truthful. All her wealth she had poured out on the path of the din; buying and freeing slaves, feeding the poor, the costs of da‘wah. In the three years of the siege that wealth had run out entirely.
blocks.24: Once Jibril (AS) came and told the Prophet {{1}}, give Khadijah (RA) salaams from her Lord and from me. And give her the glad tidings of a palace of pearl in Paradise, where there is no noise, no weariness.{{2}}
blocks.25: Many years after Khadijah’s (RA) death the Prophet {{1}} still remembered her. If someone gave a gift, he would send a share to the houses of Khadijah’s (RA) old friends. When a goat was slaughtered at home he would say, send it to Khadijah’s (RA) friends.
blocks.26: ‘A’ishah (RA) would say, I was never so jealous of any other wife of the Prophet {{1}} as I was on hearing of Khadijah (RA); though I had never seen her.{{2}}
blocks.27: The one who stays beside you in hard times, no one can ever take their place.
blocks.29: These two deaths in the same year. The Sirah has given this year a name; ‘Am al-Huzn. The Year of Sorrow.{{1}}
blocks.30: One shade was the outer; Abu Talib. Because of him the Quraysh could not openly lay a hand on the Prophet {{1}}; with the chief of the clan beside him that would bring war.
blocks.31: The other shade was of the home; Khadijah (RA). The one to whom, after bearing insults outside all day, one could put down the weight of the heart. In one year both moved away.
blocks.32: After that the Quraysh gained courage. A man on the road threw dust on the head of the Prophet {{1}}. He came home in that state. One of his daughters, weeping, washed his head. The Prophet {{2}} said, daughter, do not weep. Allah will protect your father.{{3}}
blocks.33: Such years come in our lives too. When many things break down together; a dear person goes, the job goes, the body collapses, the places of reliance slip away one by one.
blocks.34: At such a time people think, all is finished. The Prophet {{1}} did not stop that year. Seeing the door of Makkah closed he went and knocked at a new door; Ta’if. This hardship of the Prophet {{2}} was no random misfortune.
blocks.35: Once Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas (RA) asked, O Messenger of Allah, on whom does the hardest test fall among people! The Prophet {{1}} said, on the prophets. Then those nearest to them in rank, then those nearest to those. A person is tested according to the measure of his din.{{2}}
blocks.36: The year in which the most hardship came upon the Prophet {{1}} is not a sign of his rank falling; it is rather a sign of high rank. Our reckoning is the opposite. We think, if Allah loves me then life will be easy. The life of the Prophet {{2}} says, exactly the opposite can also be.
blocks.38: The Prophet {{1}} set out toward Ta’if taking Zayd ibn Harithah (RA) with him. This Zayd (RA) is that same Zayd (RA) whom the Prophet {{2}} loved like a son; freed from slavery and kept with him, and Zayd (RA), instead of going back with his own father, chose to stay with the Prophet {{3}}. On the hardest journey the Prophet {{4}} took one who had proved his love.
blocks.39: About sixty miles from Makkah, in the midst of mountains, a green town. Cool weather, gardens of grapes and fruit, the strong tribe of Thaqif. One aim only; if Thaqif accepted the din, or at least gave a safe base from which the work of da‘wah could be carried on.
blocks.40: Thaqif was one of the strongest tribes of Arabia. The fortress of Ta’if, the harvest and the trade routes were in their hands. They had an old rivalry with the Quraysh. The Prophet’s {{1}} reckoning was, if this tribe stands beside him, the siege of Makkah will weaken by itself.
blocks.41: But the leaders of Thaqif reckoned otherwise. They thought, to give refuge to Muhammad means enmity with the whole Quraysh. This risk they would not take. In Ta’if he met three chiefs of Thaqif; three brothers. ‘Abd Yalil, Mas‘ud and Habib.
blocks.42: He called them to the One Allah, spoke of Islam. One said, could Allah not find anyone but you to send! Another said, I swear by the covering of the Ka‘bah, if you are truly the Messenger of Allah then even speaking with you is dangerous for me. The third said, go, return to your own city. We will not say a single word to you.
blocks.44: The three chiefs of Thaqif had turned their faces away on the very first day. Yet the Prophet {{1}} did not leave the town. Ten days he remained in Ta’if. From one group to another, from one gathering to another; wherever anyone was willing to listen, he went and stood.
blocks.45: Not one responded. Instead the chiefs told their people, no one should listen to him. He will not be allowed to stay in our town. After ten days as he was returning, they left no final insult undone. They lined up the town’s riffraff and slaves on both sides of the road. The Prophet {{1}} walked in the middle, and from both sides came abuse, laughter and stones.
blocks.46: They threw stones in such a way that the Prophet {{1}} would be forced to jump aside; and as he moved aside another stone would strike. Zayd (RA) kept bringing his body forward as a shield. His head split and blood flowed. Stone after stone struck the feet of the Prophet {{2}}. Blood gathered inside his shoes, and when he walked his feet stuck.{{3}}
blocks.47: Having crossed a three-day road from Makkah he had come in search of a refuge. He was returning with bleeding feet, empty-handed. Standing on these very bleeding feet, a little later, he made a du‘a in which there was not a single complaint.

footnotes.0: The call of the Prophet {{1}} on Abu Talib’s deathbed ‘say La ilaha illa Allah’, the obstruction of Abu Jahl and ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah, and Abu Talib dying on the religion of ‘Abd al-Muttalib: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 1360, 3884, 4675 and 4772; Sahih Muslim, hadith 24; via Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyib from his father. ✓ Verified.
footnotes.3: Concerning Abu Talib’s lightest punishment in Hell (shoes of fire under the feet, in which the brain boils): Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 3885, 6564 and 6208; Sahih Muslim, hadith 210; via Ibn ‘Abbas and Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri (RA). ✓ Verified.
footnotes.4: Jibril’s (AS) conveying of salaams to Khadijah (RA) and the glad tidings of a palace of ‘qasab’ (pearl) in Paradise: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 3820 and 7497; Sahih Muslim, hadith 2432; via Abu Hurayrah (RA). ✓ Verified. That Khadijah (RA) is among the best women of Paradise comes in Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 3432.
footnotes.5: The remembering of Khadijah (RA) by the Prophet {{1}} even after her death, sending gifts to her friends, and the statement of ‘A’ishah (RA): Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 3816 and 3818; Sahih Muslim, hadith 2435; via ‘A’ishah (RA). ✓ Verified.
footnotes.6: Concerning the passing of Abu Talib and Khadijah (RA) in the same year (the tenth year of prophethood, about three years before the Hijrah) and this year being called ‘Am al-Huzn: Ibn Ishaq; Sirah Ibn Hisham. There is variation in the reports on the gap of time between the two deaths (from a few days to a few months).
footnotes.7: The Quraysh gaining courage after the death of Abu Talib, and the incident of dust being thrown on the head of the Prophet {{1}} on the road: Ibn Ishaq; Sirah Ibn Hisham. The narration is of the Sirah works; the chain is mursal.
footnotes.8: Concerning the hardest test falling on the prophets: Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi, hadith 2398; Sunan Ibn Majah, hadith 4023; via Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas (RA). Al-Tirmidhi said the hadith is hasan sahih. ✓ Verified.
footnotes.9: Concerning the journey to Ta’if, the rejection by the three chiefs of Thaqif, the ten-day stay, and the stoning by riffraff as he left the town and the wounding of Zayd ibn Harithah (RA): Ibn Ishaq; Sirah Ibn Hisham, 1/419–420. This detailed part is of the Sirah works; the chain is mursal. The rejection at Ta’if and its hardship are also established by a sound chain (Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 3231).

quiz.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ ask Abu Talib to say on his deathbed?
o: Subhan Allahi wa bihamdihi
La ilaha illa Allah
Allahu akbar kabira
Astaghfiru Allah al-‘Azim
quiz.e: One word, with which I could bear witness for you.

quiz.q: Which two verses were revealed in the matter of Abu Talib?
o: Surah al-Duha 3 and Surah al-Inshirah 1
Surah al-Qalam 4 and Surah al-Muzzammil 5
Surah al-Qasas 56 and Surah al-Tawbah 113
Surah al-Ahzab 45 and Surah al-Fath 28
quiz.e: ‘You cannot guide whom you love’ and the prohibition of asking forgiveness for a polytheist.

quiz.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ later report about Abu Talib?
o: His final account would be postponed
He would be in the lowest level of Paradise, without any punishment
Nothing was told about him
He would be in the lightest punishment of Hell
quiz.e: Shoes of fire under the feet in which the brain boils; yet he is the person with the least punishment.

quiz.q: The Prophet ﷺ could not make his uncle say the kalimah; what is the main reason?
o: The Prophet ﷺ did not try with enough sincerity
The work of giving guidance is not the prophet’s, but Allah’s
Abu Talib was not in a state to understand
Time to make him say the kalimah was not found
quiz.e: Surah al-Qasas 56; the prophet’s work is to convey, placing it in the heart is Allah’s.

quiz.q: Someone at home is far from the din; according to the dars what should we do?
o: Change him by force if need be
Cut off all ties with him
Be beside him, speak gently and make du‘a; the result is in Allah’s hands
Stop raising matters of the din before him altogether
quiz.e: The Prophet’s ﷺ not being able to change his uncle was no flaw in his effort.

quiz.q: Why did Abu Talib’s forty years of refuge not avail in the final judgement?
o: He had not in fact given refuge to the Prophet ﷺ
The Prophet ﷺ made no du‘a for him
In the end the Quraysh no longer recognised the refuge he gave
The worth of relations and favours is in this world, not on the plain of Qiyamah
quiz.e: In the Hereafter what will avail is dying with ‘La ilaha illa Allah’.

quiz.q: A member of the family has given up prayer; what is the first thing to do according to this dars?
o: Slowly reduce ties with him
Shame him before everyone
Stop talking about the din with him altogether
Stay beside him, behave well and keep up du‘a
quiz.e: The Prophet ﷺ tried and made du‘a for his uncle to the end.

quiz.q: Despite much explaining, someone is not returning to the din; what to do?
o: The work is as much as I can, the rest is in Allah’s hands
Blame one’s own effort and break down completely inside
Abandon his company for ever
Force him back if need be
quiz.e: Even the Prophet ﷺ could not change his uncle; that was no flaw in his effort.

quiz.q: How long after Abu Talib’s death did Khadijah (RA) pass away?
o: Within about two months
On exactly the same day
About a year later
About three years later, close to the Hijrah
quiz.e: In the same year, with a gap of about two months.

quiz.q: What did Jibril (AS) give Khadijah (RA) glad tidings of in Paradise?
o: A golden throne
A palace of pearl
A shaded orchard of fruit
A flowing clear spring
quiz.e: A palace of pearl in which there is no noise, no weariness.

quiz.q: Why could no one take Khadijah’s (RA) place?
o: The one who stays beside you in hard times, no one can take their place
She was the richest woman of Makkah
She was the eldest in age among the wives of the Prophet ﷺ
She was the mother of the first children of the Prophet ﷺ
quiz.e: When the whole of Makkah was calling him a liar, one at home was saying, you are truthful.

quiz.q: A dear one has died; many years later what is in keeping with the Sunnah?
o: To slowly stop mentioning them and forget all
To make du‘a only on the day of their death
To stop taking their name altogether
To remember them and look after their loved ones
quiz.e: The Prophet ﷺ sent gifts to the friends of Khadijah (RA) year after year.

quiz.q: By what name is the year of these two deaths called in the Sirah?
o: ‘Am al-Fil
‘Am al-Wufud
‘Am al-Huzn
‘Am al-Jama‘ah
quiz.e: The Year of Sorrow; both shades, outer and inner, moved away in one year.

quiz.q: What reality of life is recognised from the ‘Year of Sorrow’?
o: The life of Allah’s beloved servant is always easy
Even when many supports go at once, stopping is not an option
In a great calamity, suspending da‘wah is the rule
When grieved, complaining to Allah is natural
quiz.e: The Prophet ﷺ did not stop that year; seeing a closed door he went to Ta’if.

quiz.q: The hardest test falls on the prophets; what does this mean?
o: Falling into a test means rank diminishing
The prophets suffered because they sinned
Greater hardship can be a sign of higher rank
Any hardship at all is proof of Allah’s displeasure
quiz.e: A person is tested according to the measure of his din.

quiz.q: Many troubles have come together; according to the dars what should not be done?
o: Remaining patient in the situation
Seeking a new path for the work
Stopping and thinking ‘all is finished’
Seeking Allah’s refuge and help
quiz.e: The Prophet ﷺ did not stop even in the year of sorrow; he knocked at a new door.

quiz.q: Life is getting hard; according to the dars what could this be a hint of?
o: A test according to rank and measure of din
Allah has become displeased with the servant
There must surely be some big deficiency in the servant’s faith
The servant’s du‘as are not being accepted
quiz.e: The hardest test is on the prophets, then those nearest.

quiz.q: Whom did the Prophet ﷺ take with him on the journey to Ta’if?
o: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafah (RA)
‘Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA)
‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan (RA)
Zayd ibn Harithah (RA)
quiz.e: The one who chose to stay with the Prophet ﷺ rather than return with his father.

quiz.q: The leaders of which tribe did the Prophet ﷺ call in Ta’if?
o: The tribe of Thaqif
The tribe of Hawazin
The tribe of Khuza‘ah
The tribe of Banu ‘Amir
quiz.e: Three brother chiefs of Thaqif; ‘Abd Yalil, Mas‘ud and Habib.

quiz.q: What is hinted at by the Prophet ﷺ taking Zayd (RA) on a hard journey?
o: Zayd (RA) knew the roads of Ta’if well
Zayd (RA) was physically the strongest among the Companions
No other Companion was willing to go
In hard times beside you is the one who has proved his love
quiz.e: Zayd (RA) chose the Prophet ﷺ rather than return with his father.

quiz.q: In choosing a companion for a hard task, what does the dars teach?
o: Take the physically strongest in the group
Take the one who has already proved love and loyalty
Take whoever is nearest
Set out alone, taking no one
quiz.e: The Prophet ﷺ took Zayd (RA) to Ta’if.

quiz.q: On leaving Ta’if, whom did Thaqif set on the Prophet ﷺ?
o: A group of armed horsemen
The riffraff and slaves of the town
The elder leaders of the tribe
A neighbouring tribe
quiz.e: They lined them up on both sides of the road and threw stones.

quiz.q: Who was wounded in the head while shielding the Prophet ﷺ from the stones?
o: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafah (RA)
‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir al-Juhani (RA)
Zayd ibn Harithah (RA)
Abu Dujanah Simak ibn Kharashah (RA)
quiz.e: He kept bringing his body forward as a shield; his head split and blood flowed.

quiz.q: Is it right to give up da‘wah after being rejected once?
o: Yes, after one ‘no’ one should stop there
Efforts should be kept up only among one’s own relatives
No, the Prophet ﷺ tried for ten days despite rejection
After rejection one can only make du‘a from afar
quiz.e: At Ta’if, going from one group to another.
